description: In pursuit of creativity and harmony.
summary:
Harmonia is a web app that turns NASA satellite images of Earth into music, so people can hear what they cannot see.

It loads true-colour imagery from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS instruments through NASA GIBS, then divides each image into a grid of squares. Each square becomes a chord, following simple rules: brighter areas play higher notes, and mostly white areas such as clouds and ice play the highest; warm colours give major chords and cold colours minor chords; similar colours sound harmonic and mixed colours clash; and a square’s position sets whether the sound comes from the left or the right. People explore with a mouse, the arrow keys or a screen reader, or press Play to hear the whole image. A piano and meters show what is being played, and the page works in English and Portuguese.

The Earth Jukebox challenge asks for Earth science that is multisensory and accessible. 
Our project works as a new way to see images, works mixing music theory and color aspects of the image to create a sound.
We reached the objective of the challenge because we have implemented a way to translate sight into sound and this is important because the work can be used by blind people, and has much potential to expand.

Harmonia's source code, tests and documentation were written with Claude Code directed by our team. Our team defined the concept and the image-to-sound rules, chose the NASA images and tested the result. All images are real NASA satellite imagery
details:
What exactly does it do?

Our project gives a way to people interpret images, using sound.

How does it work?

The project works mixing basic music theory with color patterns. Associating details of the image with sound.

What benefits does it have?

This project can help people to see any image with the ears, including NASA vital information data.

The idea can help blind people to have an exciting experience with interpretating images with sound.

What do you hope to achieve?

We hope to achieve a software that helps people to see in a different way.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We used Claude AI to develop the code.
